report_meta.supply_chain_link: Viavi is a TEST & MEASUREMENT node in this graph — the company that tests the optics, transceivers, chips, and networks that the rest of the cluster builds. It is the 'test the network/optics' complement to FormFactor's 'test the wafer' (reports/FormFactor.json). Its NSE segment sells: LAB test (optical transport, PCIe, high-speed Ethernet, silicon-photonics test) bought by high-performance-semi makers (NVIDIA/Marvell/Broadcom), optical-module makers (Coherent reports/Coherent.json, Lumentum reports/Lumentum.json, AAOI reports/Applied Optoelectronics.json), network-equipment makers, and hyperscalers; PRODUCTION test (spectral/optical performance) for module makers — increasingly for CO-PACKAGED OPTICS (CPO), where Viavi says testing is becoming the bottleneck and 'every component must be tested at multiple insertions'; and FIELD test (fiber monitoring) for data centers (now ~40-45% of field instruments). NOTABLE: Viavi is the SIBLING of Lumentum — both were created in the 2015 split of JDS Uniphase (Viavi kept the test/measurement + optical-coatings businesses; Lumentum kept the laser/components business). Viavi also benefited from the Keysight/Spirent deal: it acquired Spirent's high-speed Ethernet test product lines (a divestiture), expanding its data-center test reach. So Viavi rides the SAME AI/optical build-out as the cluster, from the test-and-measurement angle.

beginner_glossary.Test & measurement (T&M): Equipment and software used to verify that chips, optics, and networks work correctly and fast enough. Viavi is a T&M company — it sells the 'measuring instruments' for the AI/optical build-out. (Note: T&M vendors must buy the newest chips early to build test gear, so 'early access' to silicon matters more than supply contracts.)
beginner_glossary.NSE (Network and Service Enablement): Viavi's largest segment (~79% of revenue) — test instruments and software for networks and optics: lab, production, and field testing. The AI/data-center growth engine.
beginner_glossary.OSP (Optical Security and Performance Pr: Viavi's smaller, high-margin segment — optical filters/coatings (e.g., for 3D sensing in phones) and special pigments for anti-counterfeiting (used in banknotes). Less AI-driven but very profitable.
beginner_glossary.Lab / production / field instruments: Three places Viavi's NSE gear is used. LAB = developing new chips/optics (optical transport, PCIe, high-speed Ethernet test). PRODUCTION = the factory line (measuring optical performance of modules). FIELD = out in the network/data center (fiber monitoring). All three are rising with AI.
beginner_glossary.Optical transport test / PCIe test / hig: Instruments that check very fast data links — optical transport (light over fiber), PCIe (chip-to-chip), and Ethernet (networking). AI chips and clusters push these to ever-higher speeds (800G → 1.6T → 3.2T), driving Viavi demand.
beginner_glossary.Silicon photonics / co-packaged optics (: Building optics on silicon and placing the optical engine next to the chip. These are complex to make, so EVERY component must be tested at MULTIPLE 'insertions' (test points) — Viavi says testing is becoming the bottleneck, which is good for its business.
beginner_glossary.Test insertion: A point in manufacturing where something is tested. CPO modules require many insertions (test each optical component, then again after mounting, then the finished module) because one bad part ruins the whole sealed module.
beginner_glossary.OCS (optical circuit switch): A switch that routes light directly (used in big AI clusters). Viavi expects very high market share in TESTING OCS systems.
beginner_glossary.Fiber monitoring: Field instruments that watch fiber links for faults/performance. Data centers now buy huge amounts of this — Viavi says a single AI data center can buy more than a whole service-provider network.
beginner_glossary.800G / 1.6T / 3.2T: Data-link speeds. 800G is the current high-volume workhorse; 1.6T is ramping; 3.2T is next (Viavi's first fully integrated Spirent+Viavi product targets 3.2 Tbps). Higher speeds mean more (and more valuable) test gear.
beginner_glossary.Spirent (acquisition): Viavi acquired Spirent's high-speed Ethernet test product lines (a divestiture from the larger Keysight/Spirent deal). It added a big enterprise customer base and ~$200M of annual revenue, and is the reason NSE revenue jumped ~54% YoY.
beginner_glossary.Inertial Labs (acquisition): A Viavi acquisition in inertial navigation / PNT (positioning, navigation, timing) — sensors for drones and autonomous systems. It beat its forecasts (a big earn-out was paid) and is winning U.S. Tier-1 defense programs.
beginner_glossary.PNT (positioning, navigation, timing): Technology that tells a system where it is, where it's going, and the precise time — critical for drones, missiles, and autonomous vehicles. A key part of Viavi's growing aerospace & defense business.
beginner_glossary.3D sensing: Optical filters Viavi makes for depth-sensing cameras (e.g., phone face-unlock). A high-margin OSP product.
beginner_glossary.Anti-counterfeiting (optical pigments): Color-shifting pigments Viavi makes that go into banknotes and brand protection — a steady, very high-margin OSP business.
beginner_glossary.Service provider business: Viavi's traditional customers — telecom/cable network operators. Seasonally weaker in the March and September quarters; now a smaller share as data center and defense grow.
beginner_glossary.Wireless / 6G / AI-RAN / NTN: Wireless test (5G/6G). Currently weak (down ~45%) with no near-term recovery; Viavi is focused on next-gen (6G, AI-RAN = AI over wireless networks, NTN = non-terrestrial/satellite).
beginner_glossary.Operating leverage / incremental fall-th: How much of each extra revenue dollar becomes profit. Viavi cites ~40-45% 'fall-through' on NSE — so as revenue grows, profit grows much faster.
beginner_glossary.NOLs (net operating losses): Past losses that shelter future profits from tax. Viavi has NOLs (especially in the US), so a lot of its growing profit is taxed at very low rates (Q3 effective tax ~12%).
beginner_glossary.GAAP vs non-GAAP: GAAP = official accounting (includes acquisition amortization, restructuring, etc.). Non-GAAP = adjusted. For Viavi these differ a LOT right now: GAAP is a loss (Spirent costs) while non-GAAP is a profit. Read non-GAAP for the operating picture.
beginner_glossary.P/S (price-to-sales): Market value ÷ revenue. Viavi trades ~9.6x sales. Because GAAP earnings are negative (acquisition-driven), analysts use P/S and non-GAAP earnings instead of a GAAP P/E.

company_snapshot.what_it_is: Viavi Solutions is a test-and-measurement and optical-technology company. Its big NSE segment makes the instruments used to design, manufacture, and monitor high-speed optics and networks — the 'measuring tools' for the AI/data-center and optical build-out. Its smaller OSP segment makes high-margin optical filters/coatings (3D sensing) and anti-counterfeiting pigments. It is a key 'pick-and-shovel' beneficiary of rising optical/network test intensity.
company_snapshot.founded: Created in 2015 when JDS Uniphase (JDSU) split in two — Viavi kept the test/measurement + optical-coatings (OSP) businesses, while the laser/components business became Lumentum. So Viavi and Lumentum are corporate siblings.
company_snapshot.where_it_sits_in_the_chain: Test & measurement (equipment/test tier) for networks and optics. Sells to chipmakers (high-perf semis), optical-module makers (Coherent/Lumentum/AAOI), network-equipment makers, and hyperscalers; complements FormFactor (wafer-level test).
two_segments: NSE (Network and Service Enablement) — ~79% of revenue; lab/production/field test for optics and networks; the AI/data-center engine (now boosted by the Spirent acquisition)
OSP (Optical Security and Performance) — ~21% of revenue; optical filters/coatings (3D sensing) and anti-counterfeiting pigments; high-margin, steadier
company_snapshot.recent_M&A: Spirent high-speed Ethernet test product lines (added ~$200M run rate and enterprise reach); Inertial Labs (inertial navigation/PNT for aerospace & defense, beating forecasts).

business_model.summary: Viavi makes money selling test instruments + software (NSE) and optical filters/pigments (OSP). The growth story is NSE riding the AI/optical build-out: as data links go from 800G to 1.6T to 3.2T and optics move onto the chip (CPO), the amount and complexity of required testing rises sharply — across labs (chip/optics development), production lines (module test), and the field (data-center fiber monitoring). Aerospace & defense (PNT/inertial navigation) is a second growth engine. OSP provides steady, high-margin cash. Because NSE has ~40-45% incremental fall-through and Viavi has tax NOLs, profit grows much faster than revenue.
how_they_make_money: NSE — Lab instruments: optical transport, PCIe, and high-speed Ethernet/silicon-photonics test bought by chipmakers, module makers, NEMs, and hyperscalers developing AI gear.
NSE — Production instruments: measuring the optical performance of modules on the factory line (a JDS-Uniphase legacy strength), increasingly for CPO/silicon photonics.
NSE — Field instruments: fiber monitoring for data centers and networks (data center now ~40-45% of field instruments).
NSE — Aerospace & defense: positioning/navigation/timing (PNT) and inertial navigation (Inertial Labs) for drones/autonomous systems; winning U.S. Tier-1 programs.
OSP: optical filters/coatings for 3D sensing + anti-counterfeiting pigments for currency/brand protection — high-margin, steadier.
competitive_moat_analyst_view: Legacy optical-test expertise (JDS Uniphase heritage): hard-to-replicate know-how in measuring optical/spectral performance — now in high demand for silicon photonics/CPO. [Q3 FY2026 call]
Breadth across lab + production + field: Viavi sells into the entire lifecycle of an optical/network product, deepening customer lock-in. [Q3 FY2026 call]
Early access to next-gen silicon: as a leading T&M vendor, Viavi gets alpha/beta chips before release, letting it build test gear first. [Q3 FY2026 call]
Spirent + Viavi combination: Viavi's faster hardware + Spirent's hardened Ethernet software → a leading high-speed Ethernet test platform (toward 3.2 Tbps). [Q3 FY2026 call]
OSP cash engine + tax NOLs: high-margin pigments/filters and low cash taxes fund growth and amplify earnings. [Q3 FY2026 call]

revenue_streams.analyst_view: Viavi is an NSE story (~79% of revenue) riding AI/optical test, with OSP (~21%) as a high-margin ballast. NSE's +54% YoY is part Spirent (acquisition) and part strong organic data-center/defense demand (~30-40% organic NSE growth implied). The key features are (1) the rising 'test intensity' of AI optics — more speed (800G→1.6T→3.2T), more CPO multi-insertion testing, and more data-center fiber monitoring; and (2) the operating leverage (~40-45% fall-through) plus tax NOLs that make profit grow much faster than revenue. The drags are seasonal service-provider weakness and a depressed wireless business (a potential future rebound).

competitors.landscape_summary: Viavi competes in network/optical test & measurement against Keysight (the largest T&M company, which acquired Spirent overall and from which Viavi bought divested high-speed Ethernet lines), EXFO, Anritsu, and Rohde & Schwarz. In optical filters/coatings (OSP) it competes with specialty optics makers. It is distinct from FormFactor, which does WAFER-level probe-card test — Viavi tests at the module/system/field level, so the two are complementary more than competing.

financial_performance.analyst_view: Operationally Viavi is inflecting: revenue +43% YoY, operating margin up to ~21% (toward ~23% next quarter), and strong ~40-45% NSE fall-through amplified by tax NOLs (~12% tax). The GAAP loss is an acquisition-accounting artifact (Spirent) — read non-GAAP. The model is capital-light (tiny capex) and increasingly cash-generative once working-capital/earn-out timing normalizes; management is using cash to cut debt. The story rests on AI/optical test demand (data center now ~half of NSE) plus defense, with wireless as optional future upside.

implied_multiples_analyst_view.interpretation: Because GAAP earnings are negative (Spirent acquisition costs), the meaningful gauges are P/S (~9.6x) and FORWARD non-GAAP earnings. Annualizing the Q4 non-GAAP EPS midpoint (~$0.30 × 4 ≈ $1.20) implies a forward non-GAAP P/E of roughly ~44x (management/analysts referenced ~$1.20 annualized earnings). That is a premium multiple that prices in continued AI/optical test growth and the operating-leverage ramp (toward >$500M/quarter over time). If those play out, the forward multiple compresses on FY2027 numbers; if data-center test demand or Spirent integration disappoints, the wide 52-week range ($9→$60) shows the downside.
implied_multiples_analyst_view.caveat: Don't use a GAAP P/E here (it's n/a); judge on non-GAAP earnings, operating margin, P/S, and the data-center-test trajectory.

risks.why_it_matters: ~9.6x sales / ~44x forward non-GAAP earnings after a ~6x run; recent targets are above the price but much optimism is embedded. A demand or integration stumble has big downside (52-week low $9.08).
GAAP is a net loss (acquisition amortization/restructuring); integration and synergy realization (incl. the 3.2 Tbps roadmap) must execute to justify the multiple.
NSE growth is increasingly tied to AI/data-center spend; a capex pause would hit the main growth engine.
Keysight is the larger, broader T&M leader (and the Spirent acquirer); it can compete hard in network/Ethernet test.
Traditional telecom/cable spend is seasonal and soft; wireless is down ~45% with no near-term recovery — a drag and a swing factor.
Memory and components are tight (deficit possibly to ~2030); manageable at T&M volumes but requires careful early ordering.
Convertible notes dilute the share count as the stock rises (guided ~256M shares for Q4), tempering per-share gains.
The growing A&D business depends on program wins and export-control rules (ITAR), adding lumpiness.

final_research_summary.one_paragraph: Viavi Solutions (VIAV) is a test-and-measurement and optical-technology company — the firm that TESTS the optics, chips, and networks the rest of this AI/optical cluster builds (the 'test the network/optics' complement to FormFactor's 'test the wafer,' and the corporate sibling of Lumentum from the 2015 JDS Uniphase split). Its large NSE segment sells lab, production, and field test gear for the AI/data-center and optical build-out; its smaller, high-margin OSP segment makes optical filters (3D sensing) and anti-counterfeiting pigments. The business is inflecting hard: Q3 FY2026 (reported 2026-04-29) revenue jumped 42.8% YoY to $406.8M with operating margin up 430 bps to ~21% and non-GAAP EPS of $0.27 (all above guidance), led by NSE +54.4% YoY (boosted by the acquired Spirent high-speed Ethernet lines, ~$200M run rate) and OSP +11.4%. Data center is now ~half of NSE revenue, driven by optical transport, PCIe, high-speed Ethernet, silicon-photonics test, and surging data-center fiber monitoring — and management argues that as optics move onto the chip (co-packaged optics), TESTING becomes the bottleneck (many test insertions per module), a structural tailwind. With ~40-45% incremental NSE fall-through and tax NOLs (~12% tax rate), profit grows much faster than revenue; FY2025 revenue was $1.08B (+8.4%, GAAP-profitable), and Q4 FY2026 is guided to $427–437M with non-GAAP EPS $0.29–0.31. The key wrinkles: (1) Viavi is GAAP-UNPROFITABLE on a trailing basis (net loss ~-$55M) purely because of Spirent acquisition amortization/integration costs — read NON-GAAP, where it is solidly profitable; and (2) valuation is demanding — ~9.6x sales and ~44x forward non-GAAP earnings after the stock ~6x'd off its 52-week low ($9.08→$60.43), though recent analyst targets (~$60–65, Strong Buy) sit above the ~$53 price. The facts (record-ish revenue, +43% growth, margin expansion, data-center test demand, Spirent/defense) are strong; what is debated is the durability of AI test demand, Spirent integration, and how much upside remains after the run. The core debate is valuation + integration + AI-test durability, not whether the demand exists.
